# AI and Machine-Learning UDF User Guide

This guide shows practical worksheet patterns for the highest-value AI/ML functions in version 4.0.0. The screenshots are lightweight spreadsheet mockups embedded directly as Base64 SVG images, so the guide remains self-contained.

## Configure an endpoint once

Place these settings in a small configuration area or named cells:

| Setting | Ollama example | OpenAI-compatible example |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | `ollama` | `openai` |
| Base URL | `http://localhost:11434` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` |
| Chat model | `llama3.2` | your available chat model |
| Vision model | `llava` | your available vision model |
| Embedding model | `nomic-embed-text` | your available embedding model |
| API key | usually blank | secret key or key cell |

Keep secrets out of shared workbooks. A key supplied as a formula argument is visible to anyone who can inspect the workbook. Prefer a protected local workbook, a restricted named cell, or a local Ollama service for sensitive data.

## Discover available models

Use `LLM_LIST_MODELS` before building formulas when the endpoint or model inventory is unfamiliar. It returns a vertical spill range of model identifiers.

```excel
=LLM_LIST_MODELS($F$3,$F$4,$F$1)
```

For Ollama, this reads `/api/tags`; for OpenAI-compatible services, it reads `/v1/models`. Pick a chat, vision, or embedding model appropriate to the later UDF.

## 1. Classify or summarize worksheet text

Use `LLM_CHAT` to transform free text into a concise label, structured statement, summary, or explanation.

```excel
=LLM_CHAT(A2,$F$2,$F$3,$F$4,"Return exactly one label: Billing, Access, Delivery, Other",0,16,$F$1)
```

![Chat classification worksheet mockup](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Recommended pattern: keep the system instruction fixed in one cell, keep temperature low for repeatable categorization, and send only the minimum source text needed.

## 2. Build semantic similarity directly in Excel

`LLM_EMBED` turns text into a numeric vector. Feed two resulting spill vectors into `VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY`.

```excel
=LLM_EMBED(A2,$F$6,$F$3,$F$4,$F$1)
=VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY(B2#,B3#)
```

![Embedding and cosine similarity worksheet mockup](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Interpretation: values near `1` indicate similar direction/meaning, values near `0` indicate weak similarity, and negative values indicate opposing directions in the embedding space.

## 3. Embed a list, then cluster it

Use `LLM_EMBED_BATCH` for many rows. The result is an observation-by-dimension matrix that can flow directly into the matrix UDFs.

```excel
=LLM_EMBED_BATCH(A2:A100,$F$6,$F$3,$F$4,$F$1)
=MATRIX_KMEANS_ASSIGN(B2#,H2:K5,"cosine")
```

![Batch embedding and clustering worksheet mockup](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

The centroid matrix must have the same number of feature columns as the embedding spill. `MATRIX_KMEANS_ASSIGN` returns the 1-based centroid number and distance for every input row.

## 4. Analyze an image stored as Base64

`LLM_CHAT_IMAGE` accepts raw Base64 or a full data URI. This works well for screenshots produced by another automation step, images stored in a database export, or small captured dashboard regions.

```excel
=LLM_CHAT_IMAGE(A2,B2,$F$5,"image/png",$F$3,$F$4,"Identify visible anomalies only",0,128,$F$1)
```

![Vision worksheet mockup](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Large images can exceed Excel cell-length or provider request limits. Resize screenshots before encoding and avoid including confidential workbook regions.

## 5. Apply a trained linear model

`MATRIX_LINEAR_PREDICT` computes `X × W + bias`, making it useful for imported linear/logistic model coefficients or the final dense layer of a small model.

```excel
=MATRIX_LINEAR_PREDICT(A2:D100,F2:H5,J2:L2)
```

Apply `VECTOR_SIGMOID`, `VECTOR_SOFTMAX`, or `VECTOR_LOG_SOFTMAX` to appropriate prediction rows when probabilities or log-probabilities are required.

## 6. Inspect and normalize model output

Useful follow-on functions:

- `VECTOR_TOP_K` selects the highest-scoring classes or nearest candidates.
- `MATRIX_CONFUSION` evaluates actual versus predicted labels.
- `MATRIX_CORRELATION` and `MATRIX_COVARIANCE` inspect feature relationships.
- `MATRIX_STANDARDIZE_COLUMNS` and `MATRIX_MINMAX_SCALE_COLUMNS` prepare numeric features.
- `LLM_JSON_VALUE` extracts fields from stored provider responses or other JSON data.

```excel
=VECTOR_TOP_K(B2:B20,5,TRUE)
=LLM_JSON_VALUE(A2,"choices[0].message.content")
```

## Worksheet harnesses

`Tests.xlsx` contains:

- `AIML_UDF_Tests`: deterministic assertions for all 20 vector and matrix functions.
- `LLM_Test_Data`: provider, endpoint, model, API-key, JSON, Base64, and batch-text inputs.
- `LLM_UDF_Tests`: one formula harness for every LLM UDF. Network rows report `WAIT`, `PASS`, or `FAIL`; the JSON row is fully offline.

The command-line suite in `tests/AimlUdfTests.cs` tests all six LLM functions against a local mock HTTP server, so automated tests never consume tokens or require external credentials.
